soundness_flags.label: Paired-model class, PartialDifferenceGraph, AdmissibleOrderSet, and Theorem 5
soundness_flags.one_line: LDiffPC recovery and sound orientations require diff-faithfulness, but it is absent from the model class while H is used to restrict compatible completions and to claim uniform coverage; add that assumption or prove the true SCM is retained without it.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 5
soundness_flags.one_line: The contraction clause leaves the Hausdorff metric, the distance between compatible components, the scalar asymptotic index n, and the stability modulus undefined, so its claimed rate is not a precise statement.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 1
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The proposed necessity frontier excludes irreducible components contained in any within-environment conditional-independence variety.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Any completeness result is conditional on positive-real CI-free ledger components.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The direct coefficient is identifiable trivially or by a common single-door iff Conditions C.1 or C.2 hold, under Assumptions 1–3; the proceedings theorem is numbered Theorem 10.
Proposition 2 identifies the observable image ideal by eliminating parameter indeterminates; Propositions 3–4, using an augmented target coordinate q, give the identification test.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 5, Theorem 1 and Appendix D proof
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: LDiffPC recovers the difference-graph skeleton and makes sound orientations from population regression-equality information under its diff-faithfulness assumption.
Coloured Gaussian DAG parametrizations are rationally identifiable, smooth on the positive-definite cone, and admit a localized vanishing-ideal characterization.
The paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient causal-identification criterion for MPDAGs under graph-only uncertainty.
The half-trek criterion is polynomial-time sufficient for generic identification and is paired with a related necessary condition that leaves a gap.
The paper gives complete constructive adjustment and separator criteria for DAGs and ancestral graphs, not paired covariance-ledger algebra.
The article uses test inversion for confidence sets for total effects under unknown equal-variance Gaussian DAG structure.
The article uses resampling and screening after causal discovery, then unions graph-based intervals to obtain asymptotically correct coverage for a fixed population causal effect.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct the two primary-version citations, explicitly distinguish Garcia-Puente Proposition 2 from Propositions 3–4, and state the Assaad theorem with its proceedings numbering and hypotheses.

Either add a precise diff-faithfulness assumption to the paired model class or remove H as an exclusionary constraint and prove directly that every true SCM completion remains in the confidence union.

Make the confidence-union contraction theorem quantitative: define the component-separation metric, use n_min or an explicit sequence, and state a local semialgebraic stability bound from covariance error to target-set Hausdorff error.

Run the committed four-vertex saturated order-pair audit and report at least one explicit CI-free ledger component that either exhibits an algebraic identification coincidence beyond uniform single-door or certifies its absence in that family.

recommended_next_step: Revise the source attributions and completion/coverage coherence first, then advance the four-variable component audit as the decisive novelty test for the CI-free frontier.
